title: Samlion

paragraphs: In Sotah 13b and Sifrei, Berakhah 34, Samlion says, “Moses, the great scribe of Israel, died there.” Rashi explains Samlion as a sage's name; the Arukh, under Samlion, explains it as an angel's name.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Rashi reads Samlion as a sage’s name; the Arukh reads it as an angel’s name. Both interpretations remain attributed.

The checked Sotah 13b names Samlion and calls Moses the great scribe of Israel; Rashi explicitly explains Samlion as a sage’s name. Catalogue-routed Sifrei Devarim 357, in the twenty-eighth returned paragraph, also names Samalyon beside “Moses died there,” but does not establish an exact mapping to Hyman’s Berakhah 34. The Arukh explanation remains Hyman’s attributed report, not a fresh apparatus collation or an admitted angel-person identity.
